chapter_mission: The timeline has collapsed. Days, not weeks. The wound's amplification of emotional extremes cracks the group's composure for the first time. Torin appears in a doorway with a calm warm voice — 'We need to talk about what happens when we get there' — and the argument it announces will happen later. Veraine's ship registers on long-range sensors, parallel course to Veranthos.
chapter_turn: Torin stops being an ally with a worrying framework and becomes a man who has decided. Ben does not know the content of the conversation yet. He knows the cadence. The doorway announcement is how Jacen used to open the worst conversations.

scene_plan.purpose: Cockpit. Desh converts the seal degradation rate into hours and posts the countdown on the bulkhead in a number small enough to memorise. Nobody wants to. Ben paces the common area assigning approach tasks. Torin appears in the doorway: 'We need to talk about what happens when we get there.' His voice is calm and warm and decided. Ben's stomach drops for a reason he already recognises. H16 resolves; H17 plants.

Common area. An argument about hyperspace routes stops being about hyperspace routes within thirty seconds. The wound's amplification effect hits the room — arguments louder than they should be, Sera and Kael saying sentences that are not quite theirs, Ben catching his own disproportionate anger and stopping mid-sentence. The wound is in this room now, not cosmic. Desh brings food to each of them afterward without being asked.

Cockpit, night cycle. Desh at the long-range sensor display: 'Contact. Bearing three-one-five, parallel course. It's her.' Ben overlays both trajectories — convergence at Veranthos within hours of each other. She is not fleeing; she timed this. She wants them there for the endgame. Torin watches the nav display with the expression of a man coming home and does not try to hide it. H18 plants.

relationship_turns.to: decided man — Torin's doorway announcement uses the specific cadence Jacen used before the worst conversations. Ben has the pattern now. The question is what he will do with it
internal pressure — the amplification effect is in the room. Every argument will be louder than its subject from here on. The wound is pressurising the coalition from inside
working in concert — Desh's food delivery after the argument is the first time he acts as emotional infrastructure for the whole group, not just Ben's plus-one. His minor arc is accelerating

exit_vector: Two ships converging on Veranthos. Torin's silhouette in the cockpit viewport, reflection overlaid on a sensor dot that will arrive when he does. Desh's countdown timer at hours. The group in their quarters with a pressure in their chests none of them can name. The second pinch point's clock is set.
notes: The wound's amplification of emotional extremes is this chapter's sensory engine. It must be felt as physical — arguments louder than they ought to be, fear cutting deeper, disproportionate emotion that catches its owner mid-sentence. Not possession, pressurisation (force_mechanics.implications). Torin's doorway line is the chapter's echo line; deliver once, at a quiet moment, and let its cadence do the work. Do not have Ben articulate 'that is how Jacen talked' on-page — the reader hears it through the doorway. Voice: Zahn-tight throughout; single Stover-permitted interior beat when Ben catches his own amplified anger in s2. Force phenomenology: use pressure/altitude/weather vocabulary for the amplification — the wound as atmospheric condition, not mystical force. Anti-patterns: (a) the doorway announcement is not followed by Torin's actual argument in this chapter — it is the hook for Ch21; (b) the argument in s2 should be about something trivial on the surface (routes, rotation, ration cycles) and catastrophic underneath; (c) do not show Veraine's ship directly — a sensor dot and a course overlay are enough.
